claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To begin, I need to know about your child. 

**How old is your child?**

The age of your child is important because:
- Children under 16 generally qualify automatically (subject to other conditions)
- Children aged 16-19 may qualify if they're in approved education or training
- Children aged 20 or over typically don't qualify

Please tell me your child's age.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Thanks for helping me with this. I'm inquiring about my son Alex - he's 19 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're inquiring about your son Alex who is 19 years old.

Since Alex is 19 (which falls in the 16-19 age range), he may still qualify for Child Benefit, but we need to check if he meets certain conditions.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to understand Alex's current situation. For 16-19 year olds, Child Benefit can continue if they're in approved education or training, or if they've recently left education.

**Which of the following applies to Alex?**

1. **He is currently in education or training** (such as full-time non-advanced education, A-levels, or approved training)
2. **He recently left education or training** (within the last 20 weeks)
3. **Neither** - he's not in education/training and didn't recently leave

Which situation describes Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is currently in education - he's studying for his A-levels.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Since Alex is studying for his A-levels, we need to verify that his education meets the requirements for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! A-levels are an approved qualification for Child Benefit purposes. Now I need to check a few more details about Alex's education:

**Is Alex's A-level course full-time?** 
(Full-time means at least 12 hours per week of supervised study - this includes lessons, lectures, and supervised study time, but not homework)

Also, just to confirm:
- **Is this course funded by an employer** or does Alex have an agreement with an employer for a future job as part of this education?

Please let me know about these details.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Yes, his A-level course is full-time - he's at college during the week with regular classes and supervised study sessions.

And no, there's no employer involved - it's just regular sixth form education, nothing to do with any job or employer funding.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Alex's A-level course meets all the requirements:
- ✓ A-levels are approved (non-advanced) education
- ✓ It's full-time (12+ hours per week of supervised study)
- ✓ It's not employer-funded or tied to a future job

Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check Alex's work situation.

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week (or not in paid work at all)?**

Children aged 16-19 in approved education can still work part-time, but if they work 24 hours or more per week, they wouldn't qualify for Child Benefit.

Does Alex work less than 24 hours per week (or not work at all)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Actually, Alex does work quite a bit - he has a part-time job at a local shop and works more than 24 hours a week. He fits it around his college schedule.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I see. Thank you for that information. Unfortunately, this affects Alex's eligibility for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm afraid I have to deliver some disappointing news. Based on the information you've provided, **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

**Here's why:**

Even though Alex is 19 years old and studying A-levels (which is approved education), the rule states that children aged 16 or over who work **24 or more hours per week** do not qualify for Child Benefit, even if they're still in approved education.

Since Alex works more than 24 hours per week at his part-time job, he doesn't meet the eligibility criteria.

**Important to know:**

- If Alex's working hours reduce to **less than 24 hours per week** while he's still in his A-level course, you could become eligible again and should reapply
- Once Alex completes his A-levels or turns 20, Child Benefit would stop anyway (whichever comes first)

**What happens if circumstances change:**

If Alex's work situation changes and he reduces his hours to under 24 per week while still in education, you can make a new claim at that time.

Is there anything else you'd like me to clarify about this decision, or do you have questions about any other children?
